rationale: The Latin anchors are decisive: "extende manum tuam, et extendit" (stretch out your hand, and he stretched it out) and "arcum suum tetendit" (he stretched/extended his bow) all point to the concrete, physical act of thrusting or stretching a body part outward. The Biblical citation (Mt. 12:13, the healing of the withered hand) and the medical text references confirm a literal bodily extension, matching exsert.v.01 ("thrust or extend out," e.g. "He held out his hand") over the more abstract or spatial senses.
